description:
As enterprises scale AI agents, Google is betting that idle infrastructure costs could become a major barrier to adoption. To address that challenge, the company on Thursday launched Agent Compute Engine, a service that suspends inactive agents and restores them on demand while preserving their execution state.

AI agents often spend long periods waiting for instructions, tool responses, or human approvals. While enterprises can reduce costs by shutting down the underlying compute resources, restarting agents typically requires rebuilding the execution environment and restoring context, adding latency. title: Google targets AI agents’ idle-time costs with new compute service

A certificate authority’s decision to abandon the global SSL/TLS market is exposing a weakness many organizations rarely examine: their dependence on complex PKI trust chains.

Following the compromise of private keys behind eight of its intermediate certificate authorities, eMudhra is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business and is offering customers Sectigo-issued replacements. However, analysts warn that enterprises may discover they have only limited visibility into the certificate hierarchies underpinning critical services.

The recent Google Cloud incident in London is the kind of event that should force enterprises to rethink what cloud resilience really means. Google said the disruption was caused by a “power event” affecting London-based data centers in its europe-west2 region.
